niche: a Norwegian university machine-learning group choosing which shortlisted training configuration to name in a national compute proposal for its seabed sediment classifier, forecasting each one's loss on the mapping programme's verified benchmark from a five-week pilot sweep of real training runs: an expert-label size ladder run at tabled learning rates, a learning-rate check, a few wide runs, and trials of a contractor's labels and of labels transferred from a legacy sediment map that the benchmark never scored
analyst_test: A careful but hurried analyst stitches the logs correctly, reads the learning-rate optimum off the sweeps and takes the programme's benchmark as the target, then fits one straight line in log examples to the benchmark scores of the expert-label ladder and carries it to every labelled example alike (or ranks the vendor trials on the development loss the trainer logged), so the configuration trained on all three label routes comes out best with a loss no model can reach, the ranges come from the fit's residuals, and the proposal names a configuration that scores worse on the verified benchmark than the expert-only runs.
domain_test: Every result is a scaling-study quantity the field estimates from a sweep of training runs (a score on the target yardstick for runs that yardstick never saw, the loss a noisier label route costs at matched examples and learning rate, the return to more examples past the range run, the learning rate a wider model needs, run-to-run spread, a forecast with a range for configurations larger than any run, chosen because it holds when the largest runs are held out); swap in hospital or retail nouns and learning-rate tuning by width, a development split scored on vendor labels, examples seen and seeds stop making sense.
layer1: trainer logs that repeat step ranges after a preempted job resumes from its last checkpoint
two logger versions with different column names and logging cadence
relaunched runs that share a configuration with a cancelled or diverged attempt
benchmark submissions keyed by a truncated checkpoint hash, with resubmissions and mid-run checkpoints
scheduler job attempts, requeues and cancelled jobs for one run
shard identifiers written differently by each label route, and a re-delivered shard
development item identifiers zero-padded in one export and not in the other
stakeholder_role: the group lead who signs the compute proposal

spine.entity: one logged training or evaluation scalar row of one run

world.geography: Norway (the northern coast), a national seabed mapping programme with its own compute call
world.org_type: a university machine-learning research group preparing a national compute allocation proposal

driver: A forward level for configurations larger than any yet run is read from a staged pilot in which the return per added unit was measured only on the trusted source, while the configurations to be chosen among add units from cheaper sources whose yield differs: the target yardstick never scored a run that used them, the logged score is taken on a split that includes those sources' own labels and so rewards fitting their errors, their trials ran at other settings than the ladder they are compared with, and the return to more units bends just past the range the trusted source covers, so each source's yield has to be rebuilt on the trusted yardstick at matched settings and carried forward by a form that holds when the largest runs are held out.
driver_concrete: Each shortlisted configuration's loss on the programme's verified benchmark is forecast from the pilot by scoring every final checkpoint on the expert-labelled development items calibrated to the benchmark submissions, separating at matched examples and learning rate what the contractor's and the map-transfer labels cost from what more examples return, letting that return bend as the mixed-label runs past 128,000 examples show, taking each width at the learning rate its own sweep supports, and choosing the forecasting form by how it predicts the largest pilot runs when they are held out; map labels that help a 32,000-example model then cost more than they return at a million.
stump: A careful but hurried analyst scores the vendor trials on the expert-labelled development items, sees that map labels improved the small models, fits one straight line in log examples to the ladder and adds a per-route cost read against the ladder's own runs, and names the configuration trained on every label it can get, at a forecast loss no pilot run supports; the step that lands it there is carrying the return to more examples straight past the range the expert pool covers and reading the routes' cost against runs made at other learning rates, so labels that cost more than they return at scale look like the cheapest way down.
results: R1 the pilot's finished runs and the benchmark scores that belong to a final checkpoint; R2 the benchmark loss the pilot's largest vendor-label configurations correspond to; R3 what map-transfer and contractor labels each add to benchmark loss at the same examples and settings; R4 the loss more expert-labelled examples would give past the expert pool; R5 the forecast checked on the pilot's largest runs held out; R6 the learning rate for the widest configuration; R7 the range around the named configuration; R8 each shortlisted configuration's expected benchmark loss; R9 the configuration to name and its margin over the next best
one_fact_test: a map-labelled example is not worth an expert-labelled one, and the logged development loss is scored partly on the vendors' own labels; rescues R2 and part of R3 (2 of 9): the bend past the expert pool, the matched settings, the back-test, the widest configuration's learning rate, the range, the forecasts and the pick still have to be worked
notes: strategy other: a staged-pilot scale-up forecast in which no one family carries the pick (a yardstick carried to runs it never scored, a route's cost read at matched examples and learning rate, a return to more examples that bends past the range, chosen by holding out the largest runs); calibration organ: the pilot's benchmark submissions overlap the trainer's development scores on the same final checkpoints (two yardsticks over the same runs); context artifact: the group's meeting notes that carry the shortlist; overuse.objective answered in the design note
